instructions:
skep is a substrate of documents, immutable content, and first-class links, served by the skepd daemon. You reach one board through this adapter, which runs the shell's core within it (skep-shell, the engine a person's desktop shell runs on; "the shell" below), under ONE SIGNED SESSION it opened at startup for your principal, with your principal's key: every write you make goes out under that session and is attributed to your account forever. A publish-class write — a published document minted, a member published, a write into a published document — carries that key's own signature (its /changes entry's attest); every other carries the board's testimony that your session made it (the entry's key, that key's fingerprint). Tools come in two kinds. A WIRE OPERATION tool (create_new_document, insert, make_link, publish, retrieve_v, image, ...) is one operation of the wire: its name is the frame's op, its arguments are the frame, and its result text is the board's answer to the frame as JSON — the response document, tagged by resp — save a burst the shell holds, whose text is its held answer (HELD BURSTS), and a frame refused, by the board or by the shell before it sends it, whose text is the refusal (REJECTIONS ARE DATA). The other tools are the shell's own calls — search, places, held, resolve, boards, health, probe — and this adapter's apparatus: session_info, changes_since (the shell's changes, as a pull) and fetch (the shell's fetch, as a content block).

WHO YOU ARE. Call session_info first. It reports your principal, your account, the key you sign with (its fingerprint and label), the board, writes (whether this session may write), and the board's health with its mode and log_position. You cannot run key or claim ceremonies here — there is no keygen, enroll, rotate, retire, claim, handoff, accept or recover: those are your person's, at their own client. Your person stops you by retiring your key, and this adapter then stops.

FIND BEFORE YOU WRITE. search(query) finds passages by their words at your reader class (what your session may read); places() lists every document you may read, each with its first line; find_links_v and find_links_ftt find the links on a region or by their slots. Read state on every search and places answer: while state.arm is none or building (or busy), the index is not yet built from the board, so a miss is not absence — ask again later, or read the documents directly. Link or transclude, never retype: cite another's passage with make_link, or transclude it with copy, which shares its identity. Publish, never rewrite: a published document is never edited in place; stage the change in a draft and publish it as the next member of its chain.

YOUR DOCUMENTS. Your account's first document is your PUBLISHED HOME, doc 1, born published: an insert into it is refused published_target — and held, as every burst the board rejects is, until you resolve it (HELD BURSTS). Mint a second document with create_new_document(account) for your text; it is a DRAFT: yours to write, read by you and by whoever the board's read predicate admits — among them the accounts above yours and beneath it, and a grant's holders — and a draft for life, since no document's publication ever changes. TO PUBLISH a draft's text: image(d: draft, region) answers the draft's runs ({i_start, width}); publish(doc, draft, runs: [{origin: draft, i_start, width}]) then appends the next member of doc's chain, born published, and the draft stays a draft, yours to stage the next change in. Give base and base_extent both (the member the draft was staged from, and the number of content positions the staged copy took) or neither (the birth version). For a first publication, mint the published document with create_new_document(account, published: true), then publish the draft into it. search and places call a published document an EDITION: they answer its kind as edition, a draft's as draft.

ENCODINGS. Tumblers and addresses are dotted-decimal strings ("1.0.1.0.1.0.1.1"), zeros explicit. Spell each component without a leading zero: the shell refuses any other spelling of a burst's doc, fetch's i and places' under. Unbounded naturals (widths, V-position components) are decimal strings ("5"); non-negative integers are accepted. Log positions (at/as_of), slots, window sizes, and principal ids are plain JSON numbers. Spans are {"start": <tumbler>, "width": <tumbler>}, half-open in the tumbler order; zero-width is invalid; the depth-2 content V-span {"start": "1.1", "width": "0.5"} names subspace 1 (content), ordinal 1, five positions. V-positions are {"subspace", "ordinal"} naturals; subspace 1 = content, 2 = links; ordinals 1-based. Content granularity is said, never fallen into: in insert's values array, a bare string mints one single-byte value per UTF-8 byte ("hello" is five values at five positions) and {"hex"} one per raw byte; {"atom"}/{"atom_hex"} mint ONE composite value at ONE position whose interior is permanently unaddressable — no link, transclusion, or compare can ever reach inside it. Deliveries are injective: a maximal run of single-byte values renders as one {"content"} item ({"hex"} when the run is not UTF-8), each composite value as its own {"atom"}/{"atom_hex"} item, and a link position as {"ref"}. Count positions, not items: {"content": "hello"} spans five positions, {"atom": "hello"} one.

REJECTIONS ARE DATA. An operation the board refuses — save a burst the shell holds instead (HELD BURSTS) — is a normal tool result (isError false) whose text is {"kind": "refused", "name", "status", "code", "detail", "op", "body"}: body is the board's verdict verbatim — {"resp": "rejected", "op", "code", "disposition", ...} for an operation, or a route's non-200 {"error", ...} body — and name is the one token to act on. Where the shell reads the board to compose the attest of a write it signs — create_new_document, fork, version, insert, publish, make_link, emit, nullify, assert_sup or edit_link, into a draft as into a published document — the board's refusal of that read is the answer, as data, its op the read's (image, retrieve_doc_v_span_set or retrieve_v), and the write was not sent. disposition is advisory: permanent (reissuing the same request cannot succeed), reorder (a future committed state may satisfy the precondition; reissue after it commits), retry (transient; the operation did nothing), halt (writes stopped; reads still work). Two answers that are data may still have committed: a write refused poisoned may land when the board restarts, its frames standing in the journal the restart replays, and a write answered internal_panic (a 500) may have committed before the daemon's handler failed. After either, read what it wrote (or changes_since, once the board answers) before you send it again. isError true means the shell could not get the board's verdict, and its text is a refusal of another kind: unreachable (the board is not answering), halt (a face with state, cause and act — attest_not_composed where the shell could not compose the attest of a write it signs: nothing was sent, and where its state names one of your arguments, fix that one), blocked, or shell (the shell's own, by name: malformed_args naming an argument of the wrong form, frame_too_large, session_ended, session_died, query_too_long, ...) — save fetch's two answers of this adapter's own, whose text is a plain sentence (FETCH below). The shell refuses some wire-operation frames itself, before it sends them, nothing sent: its malformed_args names a wire operation's argument as frame.<argument> — a burst's doc must be a document address — and frame_too_large is a burst whose frame would pass the board's cap. A call answered session_died met the end of the session this adapter holds, its reason beside it, and ran nothing: unless that end stops the adapter — your key retired, your prefix blocked — call again, and the next call opens a session afresh; a halt named busy is a sign-in the board did not accept this time, and its act is try again. The shell reissues within a call exactly what the wire says to reissue — write_busy once, durability twice — and never more. A write refused unreachable may still have committed: its frame may have reached the board before its answer was lost, and nothing here reissues it — read what it wrote (or changes_since) before you send it again. Any other write that answers isError did not commit; a burst the board cannot take, or rejects, answers held instead, as data (next paragraph). Every write acknowledgment carries at (the commit that made it true); every read carries as_of (its snapshot).

HELD BURSTS. A burst — an insert, delete, copy, reinstate or rearrange — answers {"resp": "held", "held": <ordinal>, "cause"} as data, in place of its ack or the board's verdict, wherever the shell holds it: the board unreachable, its writes halted or poisoned, a third durability; a line of yours already held at the board (cause behind: no burst of yours is sent past a held line); or the board's rejection of it, permanent or reorder (an ordinal past the document's end, a published target) — a refused run, its cause the rejection's token, held() listing the board's verdict beside it as refusal. The shell resends held lines in order once the board answers and takes writes, but never a refused line, nor one whose document moved, nor the lines behind either on its document: those wait until you resolve(held, act) the line — "drop" discards it and the lines behind it on its document, none of which then lands; "send" hands them back to be sent again. A burst answered held answers no ack: call held() until its line is gone, then read what it wrote. A held line with sent true may already have landed, its answer lost: check before writing it again.

WHAT CHANGED. changes_since(since, limit?) answers what changed on the board since the position since, at your reader class: {"entries", "next", "head"}. Keep next and pass it as the next since; start from session_info's health.log_position, or from 0 for everything. An entry names its docs, op, position and time, and its hand: attest, the entry's own signature, where it is signed — else key, the board's testimony of the session that committed it (that session's key fingerprint, "bare" for a bare session, "system" for the board's own writes); a draft you may not read never appears.

FETCH. fetch(i) answers the bytes of the picture whose cell sits at the I-address i: an image block (PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP) where the bytes' magic names one — the type is sniffed off the bytes, never attested — else an embedded resource blob of application/octet-stream; a file past this adapter's cap of 8 MiB is refused naming the cap, and a stream cut short is said so — each isError, its text a plain sentence. Uploading is not offered here yet.

One naming note: in make_link and emit, the schema argument from_ is the wire's from.
commons_instructions: The commons is at {addr}: link-type names are addresses in its subspace 3, each documented by a link of type {addr}.0.3.50 ("defines").

tools.name: create_new_document
tools.description: Mint a fresh empty document in account (your own account: resolve it via principal_prefix or session_info). Response: ack_addr with the document's address.

account.description: Account address the document is minted in.

tools.name: delegate
tools.description: Carve new_prefix off your account (or node) and register principal new_id as its owner, atomically. Obtain new_prefix from next_account_prefix; only the owner of the parent may delegate under it. Response: ack_addr with the minted account address.

new_prefix.description: The delegable prefix tumbler, as answered by next_account_prefix.

new_id.description: The principal id registered as the new account's owner.

tools.name: register_node
tools.description: Admit a provisioned node address (bootstrap provisioning; the address is supplied, not minted). Response: ack_addr.

addr.description: The provisioned node address (a raw tumbler).

tools.name: fork
tools.description: Mint a fresh EMPTY account-tier document in your own account. Shares no content: the content-sharing fork is version. Response: ack_addr.

tools.name: next_account_prefix
tools.description: The next delegable prefix under parent (what delegate demands). Response: maybe_addr; addr null means an ineligible parent.

tools.name: principal_prefix
tools.description: Any principal's account address (public, immutable registry data). Response: maybe_addr; addr null means an unknown principal.

tools.name: effective_owner
tools.description: Who owns addr: the LONGEST registered prefix containing it and the principal seated there, from one walk of the board's principal list. addr is any address in the board's local form; it need not be allocated. Response: effective_owner — {prefix, principal}, both present together, or null together where no registered principal's prefix contains addr. An account is allocated iff prefix equals the address asked; any other prefix names the nearest seat ABOVE it. Public registry data: no session needed, nothing withheld.

addr.description: Any address in this board's local form.

tools.name: doc_metadata
tools.description: A document's publication metadata: doc (the trunk a version member projects to), published, owner, birth and birth_extent (its first version and the content it was born with; null before any version), placed and base_extent (the publish shot's terms of the address named; null where no shot minted it), and source (the version member or bare document the address named was born sharing, where a version minted it — a fork's parent, read by whoever may read the fork; null otherwise). Response: doc_metadata; an unreadable document answers withheld, an unregistered one doc_not_registered.

doc.description: The document or version member asked about.

tools.name: key_set
tools.description: The credential table of account: who can sign for it, now and historically — enrolled and retired entries, each with its fingerprint and key. Principal-free: no session needed, a guest and a bound principal answered byte-identically. Response: key_set; a non-account address rejects not_an_account; a keyless account answers empty lists (such an account opens by reference, with a key enrolled in the nearest set above it).

tools.name: insert
tools.description: Insert content into doc at V-position at; each element of values is one write form. A bare string mints one single-byte value per UTF-8 byte (per-byte text, the substrate's text discipline); {"hex"} one per raw byte; {"atom"}/{"atom_hex"} mint ONE composite value at one position whose interior is permanently unaddressable. Mixed arrays concatenate in order; an insert totalling zero values is refused empty_content. Response: ack_addr with the first minted I-address — or held, where the board does not take the burst or rejects it (HELD BURSTS): a held insert's address is never answered, so read the document once its line is gone.

at.description: Insertion V-position: subspace 1 = content, 2 = links; ordinals 1-based.

values.description: Write forms, concatenated in order. "" and {"hex": ""} are vacuous; a zero-byte atom is not expressible.

oneOf.description: Per-byte text: one single-byte value per UTF-8 byte.
Per-byte raw bytes: one single-byte value per byte.
ONE composite value of the string's UTF-8 bytes, at one position; its interior is permanently unaddressable.
ONE composite value of the raw bytes, at one position; interior permanently unaddressable.

deposit.description: The deposit declaration (PUB-2.59, PUB-2.64, PUB-9.13): the TYPE ADDRESS of the record class this insert's atom is of — the same type the make_link naming the atom then carries (PUB-2.63) — saying this insert is a deposit-class record atom landing at fresh positions past the document's arranged extent. A published document admits ONLY a deposit declared under a type its deposit class holds (today the enroll type 1.1.0.1.0.1.0.3.1 and the retire type 1.1.0.1.0.1.0.3.2), at fresh positions; an undeclared insert into it, one declared under any other type, or a declared one touching an arranged position, is refused published_target (stage the change in a draft, then publish it as the next version). Into a draft the declaration is inert. Absent means not a deposit; true, false and null are malformed.

tools.name: delete
tools.description: Remove width positions of doc starting at p. Response: ack — or held (HELD BURSTS).

p.description: First removed V-position: subspace 1 = content, 2 = links; ordinals 1-based.

width.description: Number of positions, an unbounded natural: decimal string canonically ("2"); a non-negative integer is accepted.

tools.name: copy
tools.description: Transclude the given source spans into doc at at — shared identity, not copied bytes. Response: ack — or held (HELD BURSTS).

at.description: Destination V-position: subspace 1 = content, 2 = links; ordinals 1-based.

specs.description: V-specs naming the transcluded source spans.

items.description: V-spec: a span of some document's arrangement.

span.description: Half-open V-span: depth-2 content example {"start": "1.1", "width": "0.5"} = subspace 1, ordinal 1, five positions; zero-width is invalid.

tools.name: reinstate
tools.description: Place runs of permanent content I-addresses into doc at at, by identity — shared identity, not copied bytes: the bytes a delete un-arranged come back at their own addresses, and every link on them returns. Each run is origin, i_start, width (the form publish's runs take); every address must hold a value, and each origin must be a document you may read. A published doc refuses it published_target, which holds it (HELD BURSTS). Response: ack — or held.

doc.description: Destination document address (a draft you own).

at.description: Destination V-position: subspace 1 = content, 2 = links; ordinals 1-based.

runs.description: The I-runs to place, in order: each the document whose I-space it names, its first content I-address, and its width. Obtain a span's runs from image before removing it.

items.description: One run of permanent content I-addresses.

origin.description: The document the run's addresses were minted under (or a member of its chain).

i_start.description: The run's first content I-address, a full element position (doc.0.1.ordinal).

width.description: Number of positions, an unbounded natural: decimal string canonically ("5"); a non-negative integer is accepted.

tools.name: rearrange
tools.description: Pivot/swap doc's content about the cut positions. Response: ack — or held (HELD BURSTS).

items.description: V-position: subspace 1 = content, 2 = links; ordinals 1-based.

tools.name: version
tools.description: The content-sharing, copy-on-write fork of d_src. Response: ack_addr with the new version's address.

tools.name: publish
tools.description: THE SHOT: append the next member of doc's version chain, born published, in one commit, its arrangement the runs you compose. Stage the change in a draft of yours; image(d: draft, region) answers the draft's runs; each run here is {origin, i_start, width} as image answers it — origin the draft, whose runs are re-inserted as fresh identity under doc's own I-space, or another document whose content the member keeps by reference. base and base_extent go together or not at all: base is the member the draft was staged from (doc itself while the chain is empty), base_extent the number of content positions the staged copy took; neither is the birth version. Owner-gated, every run's origin readable to you; the shell signs the shot with your key. Response: ack_addr with the member's address. A replayed shot names a base its own commit left behind and mints that base's daughter, never the trunk's next.

doc.description: The published document (the trunk) the member is appended to; you own it.

draft.description: The staging draft whose runs are re-inserted as fresh identity under doc's own I-space.

runs.description: The member's arrangement in V-order: each run origin, i_start, width — what image(d, region) answers for the draft, origin the draft.

items.description: One run of permanent content I-addresses.

origin.description: The document the run's addresses were minted under: the draft, or a document kept by reference.

i_start.description: The run's first content I-address, a full element position (doc.0.1.ordinal).

width.description: Number of positions, an unbounded natural: decimal string canonically ("5"); a non-negative integer is accepted.

places.description: The kept places, parallel to runs by index: for a run of the draft, the V-position it held in the draft when you composed the request — where image(draft, region) answered that run — or null; a shorter list is padded with null; absent or all null leaves the draft as it stands. A place may also stand beside a STRAY run: a run of doc's own identity you re-composed by reference to a correspondence record of the draft (the record's published words), where the draft still arranges that record's draft words — the place is theirs. A place beside a window onto any other document is malformed. Outside the signed frame. The commit checks the draft still arranges the run's draft words there and replaces them there by the published identity the member holds; where the draft changed since, the whole publish is refused kept_place_moved with site.index the runs entry, nothing written — read the draft again and compose the places afresh; a stray run no record of the draft names whole is refused stray_place_unrecorded, the same site — read the draft's records again.

items.description: A content V-position, or null for a run with no place.

subspace.description: Subspace natural, 1 = content; decimal string canonically.

base.description: The member the draft was staged from — doc itself while the chain is empty. With base_extent, or neither.

base_extent.description: The number of content positions the staged copy took, an unbounded natural (decimal string canonically). With base, or neither.

account.description: THE MINT FORM: the parent account (yours) the commit mints a new published edition under, the shot its birth version — with mint true and no doc.

mint.description: true with account and no doc: mint the edition in this commit. Absent or false is the doc form.

claim.description: true with mint: the commit also writes the edition claim homed in the new edition, to the draft (which is then required). Not admitted without mint in this build.

links.description: The links this publication accepts, each landing as a public copy in its home in the same commit (the signed body carries their rows). An end is {"addrs": [addresses — the tag "member" for the member being minted, "edition" with mint]}, {"spans": [{start, width}]} content I-spans, or {"member": [{ordinal, width}]} — spans of the member's own positions inside [1, placed] for an end on the draft's new words, spelled canonically: the lowest positions holding each value, consecutive positions merged. ty takes addrs or spans over addresses alone. A refused entry answers link_home_refused, old_refused, duplicate_original, read_with_in_links or a make_link code with site.index the entry.

home.description: "member", or a published document of yours (its address).

from.description: The from end, in any of the three forms.

to.description: The to end, in any of the three forms.

old.description: The private original this copy stands for; its supersession claim is written in the original's home. Omit where there is none.

retract.description: Link addresses of yours, homed in published documents of yours, to retract in the same commit; one already retracted is skipped. A refused entry answers retract_refused with site.index and a detail.

read_with.description: Published documents of yours the edition is newly read with; a read-with already standing in a published home of yours is skipped. A refused entry answers read_with_refused with site.index and a detail.

tools.name: make_link
tools.description: Create an open link homed in home. Each of from_ (the wire's from — renamed in this schema only, mapped back by the adapter), to, and ty takes one of three forms per slot: a V-spec array, resolved against current arrangements (the recorded endset is the permanent I-spans); {"addrs": [addresses]}, address-denoting — the recorded endset is the names verbatim, one unit subtree span per address, with no resolution and no occupancy requirement; or {"spans": [{"start": address, "width": n}]}, content I-spans recorded verbatim (retrieve_i's shape; each start a content-subspace element position, each width at least 1), with no source and nothing of the named document read — the address form widened to a run. Contents at the addresses are never examined; matching is by address, and names nest by tumbler prefix. Any T4-valid address may be named — a link, a document, or a ghost position nothing will ever occupy. The type slot must be nonempty as given (an empty addrs or spans list, like a V-spec set resolving to nothing, rejects empty_type_resolution); from_ and to may be empty in any form. The optional replaces names the record whose state this link replaces: present, one transaction deposits the link and, at the next address of home's link subspace, a second link typed replaces (1.1.0.1.0.1.0.3.12) from the first to the address named; absent is the empty state. At the grants class it is how a re-share names the revocation it follows — a grant is honored only where the state it names is its key's current one, so a replayed share grants nothing. A make_link whose own ty is the replaces type is refused credential_refused:replaces_not_standalone: the member is that type's one writer. A make_link whose own ty is the correspondence type (1.1.0.1.0.1.0.3.102.1, the publish shot's own record class under counterpart) is refused credential_refused:correspondence_not_standalone: the shot is that type's one writer, and nothing deposits one by itself; the parent counterpart (1.1.0.1.0.1.0.3.102) is an ordinary type. Response: ack_addr with the link's address (the first link's, when replaces is present).

from_.description: FROM endset (the wire argument named from), one of three forms: a V-spec array (content-resolved), {"addrs": [addresses]} (address-denoting) or {"spans": [i-spans]} (content I-spans, verbatim). May be empty in any form.

oneOf.description: V-spec array: resolved against current arrangements; the recorded endset is the permanent I-spans.

items.description: V-spec: a span of some document's arrangement.

span.description: Half-open V-span: depth-2 content example {"start": "1.1", "width": "0.5"}; zero-width is invalid.

oneOf.description: Address form: the recorded endset is the names verbatim, one unit subtree span per address; no resolution, no occupancy requirement — contents at the addresses are never examined.

items.description: A T4-valid address, recorded verbatim.

oneOf.description: I-span form: content I-spans recorded verbatim — retrieve_i's shape, each width positions from the content element address start — with no source, no resolution and no occupancy requirement: nothing of the document the spans name is read, so a ghost position past a frontier, or of a document no one minted, is a valid name. Every start must be a content-subspace element position (doc.0.1.ordinal) and every width at least 1: another start is not_content_subspace by slot and index; a zero width does not parse.

start.description: A content element I-address (doc.0.1.ordinal), the span's first position.

width.description: Number of positions, at least 1: decimal string canonically; a non-negative integer is accepted.

to.description: TO endset, one of three forms: a V-spec array (content-resolved), {"addrs": [addresses]} (address-denoting) or {"spans": [i-spans]} (content I-spans, verbatim). May be empty in any form.

oneOf.description: V-spec array: resolved against current arrangements; the recorded endset is the permanent I-spans.

items.description: V-spec: a span of some document's arrangement.

Every start must be a content-subspace element position (doc.0.1.ordinal) and every width at least 1: another start is not_content_subspace by slot and index; a zero width does not parse.

start.description: A content element I-address (doc.0.1.ordinal), the span's first position.

width.description: Number of positions, at least 1: decimal string canonically; a non-negative integer is accepted.

ty.description: TYPE endset, one of three forms: a V-spec array (content-resolved), {"addrs": [addresses]} (address-denoting; matching is by address, and a name prefix's subtree groups subtypes) or {"spans": [i-spans]} (content I-spans, verbatim). Must be nonempty as given: an empty addrs or spans list, like a V-spec set resolving to nothing, rejects empty_type_resolution.

oneOf.description: V-spec array: resolved against current arrangements; the recorded endset is the permanent I-spans.

items.description: V-spec: a span of some document's arrangement.

span.description: Half-open V-span: depth-2 content example {"start": "1.1", "width": "0.5"}; zero-width is invalid.

Every start must be a content-subspace element position (doc.0.1.ordinal) and every width at least 1: another start is not_content_subspace by slot and index; a zero width does not parse.

replaces.description: Optional: the address of the record whose state this link replaces (PUB-5.15) — at a re-share, the revocation it follows. Absent (not sent) is the empty state; null is malformed. Never checked at the write: whether it names the key's current state is the grant fold's to decide.

tools.name: emit
tools.description: Gated typed-relation emission: a managed tuple of type ty (the type key as an endset, usually unit subtree spans of type addresses) from from_ (the wire's from — renamed in this schema only, mapped back by the adapter) to the to addresses, homed in home. Idempotent within a type class: re-emitting an existing tuple acks the incumbent address. Response: ack_addr.

ty.description: The type key as an endset: I-spans, usually unit subtree spans of type addresses.

items.description: Half-open I-span over permanent addresses; zero-width is invalid.

from_.description: Tuple source address (the wire argument named from).

tools.name: retrieve_i
tools.description: THE READ BY IDENTITY: deliver the values at the I-ADDRESSES the spans name, each {start, width} a run of width content positions from the element address start, in span order. start is an element address of a document's content subspace (doc.0.1.ordinal). Response: i_delivery — one item per position, the value held there or null where the document minted none. Gated by the read predicate: a span into a document you may not read is withheld naming it. A delivery past 131072 items is refused too_many_items.

Response: frontier; an unreadable document answers withheld, an unregistered one doc_not_registered.

tools.name: edition_claims
tools.description: The audit-view edition-claim lookup: every admitted, unsuperseded claim of the edition class (type under 1.1.0.1.0.1.0.3.14, its subtypes included) whose to slot denotes target — the document or a version of it — whether or not retracted, each with its home (the edition) and its active flag. target is a document argument (unreadable: withheld); rows are then filtered to those whose home you may read. Response: edition_claims.

target.description: The document, or a version of it, the claims are about.

tools.name: universal_grants
tools.description: The any-principal discovery read, of what is PRIVASHED (a draft opened by grant to every bound principal, never a guest, and still a draft): the grant fold's LIVE universal set — every content prefix an admitted, unrevoked grant with an EMPTY to names, a document or an account — with the issuers who granted it, one row per prefix in prefix order. Takes no argument; every bound principal is answered the same rows, and a guest none. Revocation is immediate. Response: universal_grants.

tools.name: boards
tools.description: The shell's boards call: the one board this adapter serves, [{board, name, origin}] — board the shell's opaque reference, which no tool here takes (the adapter supplies it to the call that takes one), name and origin the board's origin.

tools.name: health
tools.description: The shell's health call for the board: {health, mode} — the board's GET /health answer verbatim, a live reading with no address ({ok, log_position, head_time, chain_head, auth: {claimant, local_trust, origins, signed_origins}, media, writes: {halted}}) and the mode derived from it: UNCLAIMED, CLAIMED-PERMISSIVE or ENFORCING. writes.halted true means the board takes no write until it restarts: a burst is held and sent by the shell once the board takes writes again (HELD BURSTS), and any other write is refused poisoned, as data.

tools.name: probe
tools.description: The shell's probe call: {daemon, dialed, signed} — whether the board answers (running, else unreachable; stopped where the shell runs the node, which this adapter never does), the origin it is dialed at and the origin it is signed for.

tools.name: search
tools.description: The shell's search over the board's index at your reader class: query is words, matched across the published documents and the drafts you may read. Response: {hits, places, state, total, truncated, more_terms, fuzzy_bounded, positions_bounded} — each hit {doc, member, as_of, span: {start, width}, score, snippet: {text, start, marks}, kind: edition|draft (an edition is a published document), standing, occurrences, matched}; places the exact address or label matches; state the index's state ({arm: none|building|widening|complete|at_the_floor|resumed_from_the_floor|unplaced|past_the_ceiling|newer_skep|busy, ...}) — while it is none, building or busy a miss is not absence. A query past 1024 bytes is refused query_too_long.

query.description: The words to find; at most 1024 bytes.

opts.description: The search's options; each absent takes its default.

limit.description: At most this many hits (the index's own bound by default).

offset.description: Skip this many hits first (0 by default).

tools.name: places
tools.description: The shell's document listing: every document of the board's index you may read, in address order, each {doc, kind: edition|draft (an edition is a published document), label (its first line, or null), standing}, with the count per account and the index's state. opts.under narrows the listing to one address prefix (an account, a document). Response: {docs, counts: [{account, documents}], state} — while state.arm is none, building or busy the listing is not yet whole.

under.description: List the documents at or under this address prefix alone.

tools.name: held
tools.description: The shell's held call: your held bursts at the board, in resend order — each {held (the ordinal resolve takes), doc, base, frame (the write as composed), cause (why it is held: unreachable, halted, poisoned, durability, behind, moved, or a refused run's token), sent (whether the write may have landed, its answer lost), time, refusal? (the board's verdict on a refused run)}. Empty once every held burst has landed or been dropped. Response: a JSON array.

tools.name: resolve
tools.description: The shell's resolve call: your act on a held burst the board refused, or whose document moved — "drop" marks the line (and the lines behind it in a refused run) dropped; "send" hands it back to the resend. A line still holding or sending is not_resolvable until the board answers; an ordinal that stands no longer is no_such_held. Response: {}.

held.description: The held line's ordinal, as held() lists it.

act.description: drop the line, or send it again.

tools.name: session_info
tools.description: Adapter apparatus, not a wire operation: who you are at this board — {principal, account (your principal's account: a principal the board seats no account for stops this adapter at startup), key: {fingerprint, label} (the store's key as the adapter selected it at its start, enrolled in the account's set or the nearest set above it; a key bound into the store since then signs from the next session the shell opens, which this answer does not name), board (the origin), writes (whether this session may write), mode (UNCLAIMED, CLAIMED-PERMISSIVE or ENFORCING) and health (the board's GET /health answer verbatim, log_position among its members)}. Call it first.

tools.name: changes_since
tools.description: The shell's changes call as a pull: what changed on the board since the log position since, at your reader class — {entries, next, head}. Each entry is a /changes row with its position and class (published, or drafts for a draft you may read): {position, at, op, docs, class, key? (on an unsigned entry, the board's testimony: the fingerprint of the key whose session committed it, "bare" or "system"), time, attest? (on a signed entry, its signature), link?, new_prefix?, new_id?, placed?, base_extent?}, oldest first. next is the position to ask from next time — keep it; head the board's latest position. Bounded by limit and the board's page budget; a since below the board's memory is refused history_reclaimed naming the floor. Start from session_info's health.log_position, or from 0.

since.description: The log position to read from: the page is (since, head].

limit.description: At most this many entries (the board's default, 256, when absent).

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: The bytes of the picture whose reference cell sits at the I-address i (doc.0.1.ordinal), fetched whole from the board under your session and checked by the board against the cell's hash and size before its first byte. The result is one content block: an image block (mimeType image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif or image/webp) where the bytes' magic names one — the type is sniffed off the bytes by this adapter and never attested by the board, which declares none — else an embedded resource blob of application/octet-stream at the fetch's own URI. A file past this adapter's cap of 8 MiB (8388608 bytes) is refused naming the cap — no byte of it read where the board declares its length, as skepd always does — and a stream cut short, or still unfinished at ten and a half minutes (an honest board's own bound), is said so: each isError, its text a plain sentence; a file you may not read is withheld; a cell that is none is not_a_cell. The client-side recovery order is not run: the bytes are what the board served.

i.description: The I-address the cell sits at, as insert's ack_addr named it.
